I farm 600 mu, but my labor at home is limited, so I will keep the plan practical and not spread myself too thin. Because my land has well irrigation and my main system is wheat-maize, I will keep the core of the farm in that double-cropping pattern for stable grain output and cash flow. I will put 300 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 300 mu. That gives me a reliable base and fits how I already farm. On the remaining land, I will keep cotton and stevia as cash crops, but I will not expand them too much because they need more management, especially cotton for pest control and stevia for water and harvest timing. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it matters for yield stability, use moderate fertilizer instead of pushing the highest rate, rely on well irrigation to avoid drought risk, and choose tillage that matches each crop and my workload. My goal is steady output, manageable fieldwork, and lower risk rather than chasing the absolute highest yield.
